chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī from Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam from his father from Ata' ibn Yasar from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Every intoxicant is prohibited and every intoxicant is wine.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on all intoxicants in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This foundational hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), narrating directly from the Prophet (SAW), establishes the principle of 'kaff al-karam' (abundance does not dilute scarcity) in Shia jurisprudence, meaning any amount of an intoxicant renders the substance itself prohibited as 'khamr'. It serves as the primary textual basis for the absolute prohibition of all intoxicants, not just grape wine, extending the ruling to any substance that causes intoxication regardless of quantity. This ruling underscores the comprehensive nature of the prohibition in Islamic law, linking the physical effect (intoxication) directly to the legal classification.
